ILUMYA (tildrakizumab) injection for subcutaneous use is a humanized IgG1/k monoclonal antibody that specifically binds to the p19 protein subunit of the IL-23 cytokine and inhibits its interaction with the IL-23 receptor.

key_safety.text: Most common (≥1%) adverse reactions are upper respiratory infections (14% vs 12% placebo), injection site reactions (3% vs 2%), and diarrhea (2% vs 1%). Infections occurred in 23% of ILUMYA subjects. Serious risks include hypersensitivity reactions and infections.

citations.quote: Most common (\ge 1\%) adverse reactions associated with ILUMYA treatment are upper respiratory infections, injection site reactions, and diarrhea. (6.1)

Upper respiratory infections*	98 (14)	41 (12)
Injection site reactions†	24 (3)	7 (2)
Diarrhea	13 (2)	5 (1)

ILUMYA may increase the risk of infection. Although infections were slightly more common in the ILUMYA group (23%), the difference in frequency of infections between the ILUMYA group and the placebo group was less than 1% during the placebo-controlled period.
- **Hypersensitivity:** If a serious allergic reaction occurs, discontinue ILUMYA immediately and initiate appropriate therapy. (5.1)

summary.text: ILUMYA was an original BLA under section 351(a) of the PHS Act, given standard review, and approved on the basis of two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (P010 and P011) without accelerated approval or special designations.

citations.quote: Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. submitted a Biologics License Application (BLA) dated March 23, 2017 under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act for ILUMYA (tildrakizumab-asmn) injection, for subcutaneous use.
Priority or Standard	Standard

The applicant submitted data from two adequate and well-controlled trials (Trial P010 and Trial P011), which provided evidence of the effectiveness of tildrakizumab for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.
